issue.standard_remedy: Qualify a second source and shift volume
issue.summary: High-risk supplier (score 49.7) holds 19% of a category

plan.diagnosis: Everest Northern Services K.K. represents a medium-severity concentration risk with USD 173,276 in trailing 12-month spend (18.9% category share) and an overall risk score of 49.7 driven by poor ESG performance (score 33) and low resiliency (score 47). The supplier's failure class 2 rating combined with nearly 19% category concentration creates potential supply continuity exposure without adequate sourcing alternatives.

remedy_steps.step: Issue RFI to qualify 2-3 alternative suppliers in the same category within Japan or APAC region to establish backup sources
Conduct dual-source pilot by awarding 25-30% of current volume (USD 43,000-52,000) to the highest-ranked qualified alternative supplier
Negotiate improved SLA terms and quarterly business reviews with Everest Northern Services K.K. to monitor performance and resiliency improvement actions
Reduce Everest Northern Services K.K. share from 18.9% to below 12% over two quarters by reallocating USD 50,000-60,000 to qualified second source(s)
Implement monthly spend and risk monitoring dashboard tracking category concentration and supplier risk score trends

plan.expected_impact: Reducing concentration below 12% and establishing a qualified second source mitigates estimated supply disruption exposure of USD 52,000-60,000 (30-35% of current spend) while maintaining competitive pricing through dual sourcing.
kpis: Everest Northern Services K.K. category share reduced from 18.9% to <12% within 6 months
Minimum 2 qualified active suppliers achieving >15% category share each
Supplier risk score monitored quarterly with target improvement to <45 or maintain alternative sources
Category supply continuity risk score improvement by 20+ points
Zero supply disruption incidents in category during transition period
risks: Everest Northern Services K.K. may offer price reductions to retain volume, creating internal stakeholder pressure to maintain status quo
New supplier qualification timeline may extend beyond 4 weeks if technical requirements are complex or certifications required
Volume split may reduce economies of scale, potentially increasing unit costs by 3-8% during transition
Incumbent supplier relationship strain could affect service levels during volume reduction phase
Alternative suppliers in Japan market may have similar ESG and resiliency profiles, requiring broader geographic sourcing
erp_actions: SAP: Create source list entries (ME01) for newly qualified suppliers with quota arrangement reflecting target 60%/40% split in affected category
SAP: Update info records (ME12) for Everest Northern Services K.K. with volume ceiling annotations and buyer notes on concentration risk
Oracle EBS: Add approved supplier list entries for new sources and update sourcing rules to enable competitive PO distribution
Coupa: Configure supplier risk flags and spending limits (USD 20,000 per PO) for Everest Northern Services K.K. requiring approvals above threshold
All ERPs: Update supplier master data with monthly spend tracking attributes and risk tier classification for reporting
Dynamics 365/NetSuite: Enable automated alerts when single-supplier category spend exceeds 15% threshold
